title: Indian companies just raised a record $12.5 billion through IPOs, despite a falling market
sources: Siasat / PTI - IPOs in India hit record USD 12.5 billion in Jan-Sep 2026: Report
Free Press Journal - India's IPO Boom Hits Record $12.5 Billion, Bigger Issues Defy Market Slump
caption:
Indian companies just raised a record $12.5 billion through IPOs. While the stock market was falling.

Indian companies raised $12.5 billion through IPOs between January and September 2026 - the highest Jan-Sep total since LSEG began tracking this data in 1980. This happened even as the Nifty 50 fell nearly 14% and foreign investors sold roughly Rs 2.7-3 lakh crore of Indian equities - domestic investors kept buying. Deal count fell to 220 issues, down from 268 a year earlier - fewer IPOs, but much bigger ones, led by NSE's own Rs 22,561 crore listing, India's second-largest IPO ever.

Fewer companies went public this year. But the ones that did raised more money than any January-to-September period on record.

Sources: Siasat/PTI, Free Press Journal, citing LSEG data (2026)
